unit.why: A single narrative: before R. Elimelech joined the Hasidim, his brother R. Zusha tells him a parable of the king and the stoker, and as a result Elimelech travels to the Maggid of Mezeritch.
unit.boundary_note: The text contains running page headers ('מהצה״ק רבי ר׳ אלימלך מליזענסק') and a page number inside it.

stories.start_quote: הצה״ק ר״א בטרם הסתפח לחברת החסידים
stories.end_quote: נסע הה״ק מהר״א להמגיד הק' ממעזריטש ז״ל
stories.summary_en: R. Elimelech, then a non-Hasidic scholar, asks his brother R. Zusha why he behaves so oddly; Zusha answers with a parable of a stoker who gives up his wealth to watch the king through a hole and of the king's banished son, applies it to their two paths, and Elimelech then goes to the Maggid of Mezeritch.

quotes: אחי אספר לך מעשה נפלא למען תדע
כבלות מהר״ז המשל הזה לאחיו הקדוש
tags.why: The core of the story is a mashal told by R. Zusha.
Elimelech, not yet a Hasid, is drawn to the Maggid through the events.
